Messages.Author: wes
Messages.Body:
I know this has been covered before, but I need an official confirmation for
a JOL game (149) where this just came up.
--------------------------------------------------------------

Lucita bleeds (at inherent 0 stealth) and her prey tries to block with a
Sabbat minion of capacity less than Lucita, ie younger. The blocking
methuselah claims that because bleeding is by default at 0 stealth, Lucita's
special ability does not apply to her blocking minions, whose inherent
intercept is also at 0. Assume there are no other eligible minions available
to block in this case.

The moderator of JOL149 thinks that the blocking methuselah is correct
because no errata has been posted about Lucita. I believe that this is a
case of confusing text more than anything else. The '-1 Intercept' from
Lucita's ability is in this case the same thing as giving her '+1 Stealth'
for all intents and purposes.

Also, there is no need for errata in this case for either Lucita or the
stealth/intercept rules themselves because a vampire's inherent level of
stealth or intercept is indeed able to go below 0, rather than always being
greater than or equal to 0. The blocking Sabbat vampire in this particular
case starts at a default of -1.

Please excuse excessive verbosity... thanks in advance
WES

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
"wes" <gh...@mnsi.net> writes:

> Lucita bleeds (at inherent 0 stealth) and her prey tries to block with a
> Sabbat minion of capacity less than Lucita, ie younger. The blocking
> methuselah claims that because bleeding is by default at 0 stealth, Lucita's
> special ability does not apply to her blocking minions, whose inherent
> intercept is also at 0. Assume there are no other eligible minions available
> to block in this case.

Their intercept can go to less than 0. Intercept starts at 0, but it
can (like the stock-market) go up or down.
